formula_checks.name: whyNoReturn
formula_checks.why: The sentence branches cover the known refusal conditions, but they do not state a priority when multiple conditions occur together, and “value less than money added” can be caused by a legitimate same-day withdrawal or by incomplete records.
formula_checks.should_be: Use one deterministic priority order; name the exact missing/invalid record and refuse the return rather than silently picking one reason.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule DEC-1669 and DEC-3035i; tenet 8.

formula_checks.name: mortgagesByProperty
formula_checks.why: The matching heuristic can leave mortgages on no property or allow more mortgage records than properties. That may be useful as an error report, but the owner rule says no mortgage without a property and never more mortgages than properties; the card does not say these are invalid-data diagnostics rather than accepted state.
formula_checks.should_be: Validate the invariant, match every valid mortgage to a named property, and report unmatched/duplicate mortgages as errors requiring correction rather than a normal valid mapping.

formula_checks.name: propertyUses
formula_checks.why: It treats a stored “rental” use as rental when no rent entries are handed in. DEC-1926 says a property is a second/vacation home unless rental income is entered on the Income screen; DEC-3035p says rental only when an entry names it. Missing rent records must not silently preserve rental status.
formula_checks.should_be: A property is rental only when a live rent entry names it. Use the shared home-selection rule for the one home; all others are second homes. If rent data are unavailable, distinguish unavailable from confirmed no rent entries.

formula_checks.name: taxWordsOf
formula_checks.why: The wording gives fixed treatment for 529 and HSA and only adds “(Roth)” for tax-free accounts in the Roth bucket, matching DEC-3035c.

formula_checks.name: holdingClassOf
formula_checks.why: It preserves the person’s answer, keeps asked/unresolved holdings Unclassified, then applies the safe name evidence needed for money-market funds, CDs and T-bills, and never defaults unknown holdings to stocks.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-2484r, DEC-3035f, DEC-3035g, DEC-3035o.

formula_checks.name: primaryHomeIdOf
formula_checks.why: It delegates to propertyUseMap and correctly distinguishes no home (null) from not being asked, but the “first entered” rule must agree with the phrase “last in the list” in F-117. The order of records/list is not defined here.
formula_checks.should_be: Return the property selected by the shared propertyUseMap; explicitly define the insertion order and ensure all property functions use the same one.

formula_checks.name: assetsStateFrom
formula_checks.why: An absent saved record or empty saved account list returns no state rather than a $0 portfolio with an invented blended return.

formula_checks.name: yearlyInterest
formula_checks.why: The formula returns “nothing” when rate is missing, but the owner’s rule says a bond/CD with no rate entered counts as $0 annual interest and the app says so. The note in the card itself contradicts its formula.
formula_checks.should_be: Return $0 annual interest when rate is missing and expose a disclosure that the rate was not entered; if rate exists, use face×rate or value×rate when face is absent. Do not invent a yield.

formula_checks.name: altPartsOf
formula_checks.why: Alternative portions are assigned by holding kind and remaining value, but any remainder is always “other” even if the account contains an alternative holding whose class is known but price is missing. It does not specify how to handle missing sync prices without presenting an incomplete total.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the same class split for total and per-kind rows; allocate known priced portions and flag unknown/missing portions rather than silently labelling them “other” unless “other” is genuinely the confirmed kind.

formula_checks.name: rentAmount
formula_checks.why: “0 when none” conflates no rent entry with an absent/unavailable rent amount. Under the tenets, unknown is not zero; a missing field must not look like confirmed zero rent.
formula_checks.should_be: Return the entered numeric rent; distinguish explicitly no rent from missing/unavailable rent data, and only use zero for a confirmed no-rent entry.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1926 and DEC-3035p; tenet 3.

formula_checks.name: liveRent
formula_checks.why: It keeps rent entries with income or costs above zero, but does not state how malformed amounts, negative amounts, or missing amounts are handled. An entry with costs only is live; that is likely intended but needs edge coverage.
formula_checks.should_be: Include entries with a known positive incoming-rent or cost amount; preserve the difference between zero and missing/unparseable values.

formula_checks.name: rentedIdsOf
formula_checks.why: It returns property IDs named by live rent entries, which lets the shared property-use rule use the actual Income-screen linkage.

formula_checks.name: propertyUseMap
formula_checks.why: The formula uses the first-entered property but parenthetically says “last in the list”, which conflicts with DEC-2747e’s “entered first” unless the list is reverse chronological. It also allows a stored rental to remain rental when no rent entries were handed in, conflicting with DEC-1926/DEC-3035p.
formula_checks.should_be: A live rent entry naming a property makes it rental. Otherwise the one marked home is home; if none marked and no use stated, select the genuinely first-created property using a clearly defined ordering; every other property is a second home. Never infer rental solely from a stored rental label when no Income entry names it.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1926, DEC-2747e and DEC-3035p.

formula_checks.name: itemizeMissingCount
formula_checks.why: It counts missing or nonnumeric holding values and marks the remainder nonfinal whenever any are missing, preventing an incomplete itemization from looking complete.

formula_checks.name: estimatedAccrued
formula_checks.why: The accrued-interest formula is correct for a simple annual coupon schedule, but it assumes the last maturity anniversary is the last coupon date and needs explicit treatment of leap-day anniversaries/day-count conventions. It also requires rate above zero, while an explicitly entered 0% rate is known and yields $0 accrued interest, not unknown.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the actual coupon schedule/day-count basis; a known zero coupon gives zero accrued interest, while missing rate/face/date refuses. Keep CDs, matured bonds and coupon day at no estimate.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision DEC-3390; ordinary accrued-interest arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: theBonds
formula_checks.why: Sorting is correctly soonest maturity first with undated last, and CD sensitivity is suppressed. The summary inherits the missing-face-as-zero issue from bondSummary; the orchestrator must not show a complete face total when some faces were never entered.
formula_checks.should_be: Preserve sort order and disclosures for bonds omitted from average yield; total face value must identify missing face values rather than silently treating them as zero.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1558, DEC-2484b and DEC-2748b.

formula_checks.name: theAccount
formula_checks.why: The card explicitly says no figure only when there are no records at all; with a record whose amount is $0, the income sum is $0.

formula_checks.name: theNetWorth
formula_checks.why: The arithmetic definitions of assets/debts/net worth and class splits are clear, but the orchestrator sums every account balance despite the owner rule that missing balances are not zero and must be named. It must also reconcile mortgages and class rows to the same total.
formula_checks.should_be: Sum known asset/debt balances and flag each missing value; class rows and totals must reconcile; cash + investments + property = owned total only when the class data are complete; return must remain TWR and refuse on missing movement-day values.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1925, DEC-3146, DEC-3279e and DEC-1669.

formula_checks.name: theEmergencyFund
formula_checks.why: The emergency-fund equations correctly count rent and debt minimums, exclude voluntary above-minimum payments, and avoid double-counting mortgage budget lines. However, when rent is equal to or exceeds essentials it clamps monthly draw to zero and refuses months-covered, which is sensible, but the formula must ensure the same net rent row is used across screens and distinguish missing income/rent data from confirmed zero.
formula_checks.should_be: Use cashTotal, essential expense average over months with logged entries, debt minimums, net rental income from the same Income summary figure, and refuse months covered when draw is zero; explicitly flag missing data and preserve the same rent figure everywhere.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1668, DEC-1925 and DEC-1926; tenet 4.

formula_checks.name: theAlternativesOutlook
formula_checks.why: The summary reads the same alternative portions and weighted rates as alternativesSummary, refuses growth when nothing is held, and rows should add to the total.

formula_checks.name: theHolding
formula_checks.why: The holding-detail calculations are broadly specified, including FIFO cost lots and a one-share day change. It does not explicitly say how negative/zero total paid, duplicate sale records, or missing share price should be validated; no-price value equals total paid is a useful cost basis display but must not look like market value.
formula_checks.should_be: Use FIFO for sales; preserve separate cost, market value, realized/unrealized gain; no price means value is shown as cost basis and gains/return/tax estimate refuse; label it plainly as not current market value.

formula_checks.name: theLookBack
formula_checks.why: The orchestrator is a pass-through to lookBack, but the card does not include the lookBack formula, output contract, or refusal behavior. The general brief says do not judge formulas of dependencies not in the batch, but here even the delegated function contract is absent from this card.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card formula only; dependency contract absent.

formula_checks.name: thePerformance
formula_checks.why: The orchestrator contains many coherent invariants: recorded beginning is read, money moved is separated, transfer between measured accounts nets to zero, dividends/interest are included in wealth generated, and TWR is required. However, it back-solves a beginning when no record of these accounts exists, then says no percent is given; that may be acceptable for a dollar walk but risks implying an observed beginning. It also says missing account value on a recorded day is not used, while other logic says a typed balance stands until next record; clarify interaction.
formula_checks.should_be: Never show a back-solved beginning as observed; label it inferred or omit the walk. Keep TWR refusal conditions, show ending independently, and apply one consistent carry-forward rule for missing account rows. Do not compute a percent when no valid beginning/flows are recorded.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1669, DEC-3035i and the approved Performance v17 drawing.

cases.name: theEmergencyFund
cases.title: Rent data unavailable is not confirmed zero
cases.given: Cash $10,000, monthly essentials $2,000, but Income-screen rent data could not be loaded.
cases.expected: RULE UNCLEAR — no runway figure until rent data availability is resolved; if rent is confirmed $0, months covered is 5.
working: If rent is confirmed zero, monthly draw = $2,000 and runway = 10,000/2,000 = 5 months.
Unavailable rent data is not proof of zero rent.
cases.rests_on: Owner decisions DEC-1668 and DEC-3035p; tenet 3.
cases.notes: The case distinguishes unavailable income data from a confirmed no-rent household.
cases.formula_gives: If unavailable rent collapses to 0, the formula gives 5 months; that number is not justified until rent data availability is resolved.

cases.name: theHolding
cases.title: FIFO sale consumes oldest lots
cases.given: Buy 10 shares at $10 on Jan 1; buy 10 at $20 on Jun 1; sell 12 shares in Sep.
working: FIFO: first 10 shares cost $100; next 2 cost $40; total cost sold $140.
Sale proceeds = 12×25=$300.
Realized gain = $300 − $140 = $160.
Remaining 8 shares are from second lot, cost 8×20=$160.
cases.notes: Expected realized gain corrected by arithmetic: $300−$140=$160.
